claims.text: Incorporating a controlled amount of Mo into an HEA coating promotes in-situ formation of MoO2 during sliding.
The in-situ MoO2 layer simultaneously reduces coefficient of friction and wear rate over a wide temperature range.
Multi-target magnetron co-deposition can produce a Mo-modified (AlCrTiZrMox)N coating.
Frictional heating in an oxygen-containing environment can trigger localized oxidation of Mo in the coating.
Mo incorporation causes the coating to develop a columnar microstructure.
The proposed columnar microstructure facilitates localized oxidation of Mo during friction.
Friction-induced shear and localized heat promote oxidation of incorporated Mo to MoO2.
MoO2 forms a layered, easy-shear tribolayer.
The MoO2 tribolayer reduces direct contact between the sliding bodies.
The MoO2 tribolayer lowers interfacial shear forces.
Mo modification improves the hardness and toughness of the coating.
The proposed improvements in hardness and toughness retard coating wear.
Mo incorporation will reduce the friction coefficient by approximately a factor of 2–3 relative to the Mo-free coating.
Mo incorporation will lower wear rate by up to one order of magnitude relative to the Mo-free coating.
The predicted friction and wear improvements will persist from room temperature to elevated service temperatures.
The intervention requires sufficient frictional heat and oxygen availability to remain effective.
Very low oxygen availability can prevent Mo oxidation and limit the intervention's effectiveness.
Corrosive atmospheres that dissolve or rapidly degrade MoO2 can limit the intervention's effectiveness.
